Shaheed Mohammad Ali Nadhar: A Heart That Carried Water to the Thirsty, and a Soul That Journeyed to Martyrdom #martyrs_stories @BasiraPress In the heroic epic of Ali al-Taher, where courage stood firm against overwhelming odds, a young man named Mohammad Ali Hisham Nadhar wrote his own chapter of Karbala. He was not merely a fighter; he was a devoted companion whose courage found expression in service, sacrifice, and unwavering faith. Like Abu al-Fadl al-Abbas (AS), the standard-bearer of loyalty and the one who ventured towards the river to bring water to the thirsty, Shaheed Mohammad (ra) undertook a mission of care amid the fiercest moments of battle. He carried water and food to the fighters, sustaining those who stood on the front lines. Under the weight of danger, he never abandoned his responsibility. His hands carried provisions, but his heart carried an entire battlefield's worth of devotion. Before departing for his final mission, he bid farewell to his family and asked his mother to remain strong, even as tears filled her eyes. His face, his father recalled, radiated a remarkable light. For two and a half months, his family lived between hope and heartbreak, not knowing whether he had been captured or martyred. Then, on the day commemorating the martyrdom of Sayyedah Fatimah al-Zahra, the news finally arrived: Mohammad had attained martyrdom. His body was absent, but his legacy returned home. He departed as a young man, but left behind the stature of a hero: courageous like Abbas, devoted like Ali al-Akbar, and faithful until his final breath. Some carry water to keep their brothers alive. Others give their lives so that an entire cause may live on. Mohammad Ali Nadhar did both. Al Fatiha 🥀

🚜 The implementation of Law 185 on Agricultural, Livestock, and Forest Land, in effect since September 17, 2026, has resulted in 5,333 applications covering 137,500 hectares throughout Cuba, of which 131,000 have already been granted under provisional administration to nearly 4,000 producers, according to Raúl Placencia Quintero, director of Land Affairs at the Ministry of Agriculture. 📋 As part of the country’s economic and social transformations, the process has seen the highest demand in the provinces of Villa Clara, Santiago de Cuba, and Camagüey, in addition to 29 applications from micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) and allocations managed by 88 Agricultural Production Cooperatives (CPAs). 🏡 The regulations grant access to land—with no limits on size or duration—to Cuban citizens, residents abroad, and foreigners living on the island, and also authorize the construction of homes that can be legalized after five years.

🚨 Hundreds of riverside families and members of the Xikrin and Arara Indigenous peoples are facing a health emergency in the Volta Grande do Xingu region of Pará state due to the presence of a green bloom of algae and cyanobacteria—known locally as “abacatada”—in the Bacajá River and its surrounding areas. 🧪 On Wednesday, November 18, the MATI-VGX Institute reported that approximately 30 kilometers of the Bacajá River, the Pariaxá Stream, and sections of the Xingu River in the municipalities of Anapu and Senador José Porfírio were contaminated with potentially toxic cyanobacteria. ⚡ For its part, the private company Norte Energia stated that its technical analyses do not link the phenomenon to the Belo Monte hydroelectric plant and asserted that recent monitoring shows a reduction in the concentration of these microorganisms.
